summary: Atmospheric pressure atomic layer epitaxy (AP-ALE) of ZnS is reported using Zn and H2S. The growth rate is controlled by the self-limiting process, and the ALE growth of ZnS is achieved in the substrate temperature range of 350—500°C. The study demonstrates the feasibility of AP-ALE for producing high-quality ZnS epitaxial films.
evidence: Atmospheric pressure atomic layer epitaxy (AP-ALE) of ZnS is reported for the first time using Zn and H2S. It is confirmed that the growth rate is controlled by the self-limiting process itself. The ALE growth of ZnS is achieved in the substrate temperature range of 350—500°C and in the input partial pressure ranges of 2.6×10−5—9.1×10−5 atm for zinc and 2×10−4—2.4×10−3 atm for sulphur. The purpose of this paper is to describe the ALE growth of single-crystalline films of ZnS on GaP under conditions of atmospheric pressure using Zn metal for the group II source and H2S gas for the group VI source.
